Kyrgyzstan Ends State-Backed Stablecoin Project Months After UK Sanctions

Kyrgyzstan has decided to shut down USDKG, its $50 million state-backed gold stablecoin project, and ordered the liquidation of issuer EVA and Coin Nomad Exchange, the country's first state-owned crypto exchange. Launched in November 2025, USDKG was pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and backed by physical gold, primarily for cross-border payments. The UK sanctioned its issuer in May 2026 over alleged support for Russia. — link

Cointelegraph Seeks Buyer as Traffic Plunges From 12 Million to 700K Visits

Cointelegraph, one of the largest and longest-running crypto news outlets, is seeking a buyer after a Google manual penalty in October 2025 reportedly slashed its organic search traffic by around 80%, according to CoinDesk. Similarweb data show monthly visits plunged from over 12 million in December 2024 to just above 700,000 by early September 2026. Founded in 2013 and employing more than 200 people, Cointelegraph has not disclosed an asking price or responded to requests for comment.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin warned that AI could accelerate mathematical advances enough to weaken lattice-based cryptography, including ML-DSA and FHE, within two years, potentially putting ECDSA at risk sooner than expected. He said Ethereum’s Lean roadmap is shifting toward hash-based signatures to reduce these risks. Kalshi Asks CFTC to Approve a Never-Expiring WTI Crude Futures Contract

Kalshi has filed a proposal with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for a never-expiring futures contract tied to the WTI crude benchmark, Bloomberg reported. If approved, it would be the first crude oil perpetual traded on a US-regulated platform. The CFTC has 45 days to approve or reject it. The contract is planned to trade 24 hours a day, five days a week. Kalshi’s commodity-market volume was close to $400 million as of early September. — link
